title: my algo performance so far really proud!
author: Significant-Lion5275

comments.author: Foreign-Safe-8161
comments.body:
Ah, the classic 'Vor Gebühren & Slippage' fine print—the magical land where every strategy is a money printer!  
Seriously though, with a \~40% win rate on high R:R setups, execution friction is going to eat those R-multiples alive once real fills and exchange fees hit the account. Looks clean on paper, but the real market is a brutal accountant

replies.author: Significant-Lion5275
replies.body:
we'll see!! so far it has been working fine for 3 months in a row let's see if it hols up to that during septembers contract change! 

Fair point regarding the friction! However, the $125 (137,50$ with commissions) per R calculation already accounts for a conservative average net target. We run this on institutional data feeds (DXfeed) where slippage is minimized, and even with standard commissions factored in, the strategy safely maintains its edge over a high sample size. The proof is in the live executions we share daily

replies.author: Foreign-Safe-8161
replies.body:
Fair enough, will definitely be interesting to see how it holds through the September roll!

Just a small quick heads-up on execution dynamics though: standard data feeds like DXFeed definitely cut down on data latency, but they don't buy you queue priority or remove execution slippage at the matching engine level—that's physical order book depth at work when market orders cross the spread.

Still, if your real fills are matching backtest expectations, respect for putting it to the test on live funds. Good luck with the rollover!

replies.author: Significant-Lion5275
replies.body: thanks man, appreciate the tips and kind words! I'll try to keep updating you guys! We actually do use the algo on our own money but not in huge amounts only 4-5 digit numbers we can loose! :))
